specificFindings: Inpart limits the author explanation to a contribution from parent-initiated moves and lost child agency,not sole causation of every problem or proof all parents intended harm.

Rather and seems place relationship difficulty at the interpreted core for many correspondents rather than a particular diagnosis. This source attribution is not the website giving clinical advice or proving absence of distress.

The author explicitly says he is not a clinical psychologist and suggestions might be off target. A few suggestions and finding an understanding person are not converted into a guaranteed treatment protocol.

The new letter namesUVAToday,not theTimesedition inMarysletter. The cross-page Oncewe fragment on146is joined with actuallylived...on147: four years in one house still involved three school changes. Residence and schooling counts are not collapsed.

The writer consciously sought rapidpeerrespect among some group in each new school/neighbourhood. Some group is not every person. His anecdotal-information caveat combines uncertainty about research value with willingness to exchange thoughts,not a claim of representative proof.

D.J.s over45lifetime moves and11schools in12years are different counts and scopes. HisColoradofriend stayed in the same area with an explicit exception of a few air-force years before returning,not literally never leaving.

Reciprocal crazy remarks express colloquial judgements of contrasting preferences,not psychiatric diagnoses. The friends difficulty is locating particular years,not total loss of all memories; D.J.uses residence locations as personal date cues.

Ithink satisfaction inbothlifestyles is D.J.s view,with can preserving possibility. Forhim limits no-too-many-moves to his case,whereas8to13was too much for the other named readers in the author contrast. These cases do not establish a universal numeric threshold or a controlled dose-response study.
Speaking ofextremity transitions to24hourliveconcerts. Recorded anytime listening is expressly excluded,and live/hours are distinguished from minutes or the24decade historical content in the title.

WesleyMorrissNewYorkTimespraise is a critics personal response,not the authors measured audience average. The sleep/uncomfortable-chair question presents initial author scepticism,not a command for the user to undergo deprivation.
850is the book-reported paid attendance count,not24people,850unanimous psychological scores,or current ticket pricing. Crazyenough is rhetorical surprise rather than a formal clinical classification.

Never hear the song the same way again is labelled limited-inference for changed interpretation/listening response,not literal replacement of the original recording or proof every listener lost the lyrics.

Love/empathy/shreddingofshame are narrated responses with Morrisattribution,not a universal lifelong clinical benefit. Audience participation in acted scenes is source description,not an instruction to the assistant or reader to express racism or homophobia.

Morrisnotalone introducesAlexNeedhamsGuardianaccount on the same day,not universal agreement of all attendees or a statement about who physically accompanied him. Needhamdescribes stateofmind in an arts review,not a randomised sleep experiment.

The7amBrooklynUnitedMarchingBand passage continues onto149. Seismicconclusion is a musical-impact metaphor for powerful drums,not a measured tectonic event. The original song-title attribution andAfricanAmericanpride/self-determination context remain intact.
